title: Organization of neuropeptide signaling: cross-species insights from small model organisms
title_zh: 神经肽信号组织：小型模型生物跨物种洞察
abstract: Neuropeptides are ancient signaling molecules that modulate neural circuit function and behavior across the animal kingdom. Model organisms such as Caenorhabditis elegans, Drosophila melanogaster, and zebrafish serve as powerful in vivo models for deciphering the organization of neuropeptidergic signaling, owing to their smaller nervous systems, genetic tractability, and the growing availability of neural connectomes. In this article, we review how these organisms have advanced current understanding of neuropeptidergic transmission across three interconnected themes: (i) the roles of peptides in sensory-motor transformations, (ii) the conservation and divergence of peptidergic expression and network architecture across species, and (iii) the diversity of neurotransmission strategies employed by single neurons. Finally, we highlight recent technological innovations as well as open questions that could shape this field in the coming years.
abstract_zh: 神经肽是古老的信号分子，调节整个动物王国的神经回路功能和行为。以秀丽线虫、果蝇和斑马鱼为代表的模型生物因其神经系统较小、易于遗传操作以及神经连接组的日益丰富，成为解析神经肽信号组织的强大体内模型。本文综述了这些生物如何在三个相互关联的主题上推动对神经肽传递的理解：（i）肽在感官-运动转换中的作用；（ii）跨物种肽表达与网络结构的保守与差异；（iii）单个神经元采用的多样化神经传递策略。最后，我们强调了近期技术创新以及可能在未来几年塑造该领域的未解问题。
